stories.title: Rich Development Trades Newly Built Shopping Center
stories.excerpt: Hanley Investment Group Real Estate Advisors recently arranged the sale of Apple Valley Towne Center, a newly built 87,042-square-foot regional shopping center located at 19390 Bear Valley Rd. in Apple Valley. The center is 100% occupied by three national junior box tenants, Hobby Lobby, Marshalls and Five Below, and is shadow anchored by Stater Bros. Markets, Lowe’s Home Improvement and Walgreens. EVPs Kevin Fryman and Bill Asher, along with SVP Sean Cox, represented the seller and developer, Rich Development Enterprises of San Pedro. The buyer and purchase price were not disclosed. “We listed the property before the tenants opened for business, which gave the center early exposure and generated strong interest from private, mid-market and institutional investors,” said Fryman. “Presenting the assets both individually and as a three-tenant package expanded the buyer pool.” Completed in 2026, Apple Valley Towne Center features new long-term triple-net leases with scheduled rental increases every five years. The post Rich Development Trades Newly Built Shopping Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Rich Development sold newly built 87,042-sf Apple Valley Towne Center, 100% leased to Hobby Lobby, Marshalls, Five Below.
Property completed 2026 in Apple Valley, CA with triple-net leases featuring 5-year rental escalations.
Strong investor demand—private, mid-market, institutional—for newly stabilized retail with long-term lease certainty.
stories.summary: Rich Development Enterprises sold Apple Valley Towne Center, a brand-new 87,042-square-foot regional shopping center in Apple Valley, California, fully leased to three national junior box tenants with shadow anchors. The property, completed in 2026, features long-term triple-net leases with scheduled rental increases every five years. Hanley Investment Group brokered the off-market sale, which generated strong institutional and mid-market investor interest.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Retail property sale signals healthy investor appetite for newly stabilized assets with long lease terms and rental escalators, but no multifamily supply, demand, or capital implications.

stories.title: Doug Middleton to Lead New York Institutional Capital Markets at Cushman & Wakefield
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield has hired Doug Middleton and Jack Stillwagon to lead its Institutional Capital Markets business across New York City. Joining from CBRE, Middleton and Stillwagon bring extensive experience in sourcing and executing transactions for large commercial assets across New York City. At Cushman & Wakefield, they will also collaborate with capital markets teams across the country. Middleton joins the firm as executive vice chairman. For the past eight years, he led CBRE’s Investment Properties Institutional Group in New York City, following his role as director of investment sales at Eastdil Secured. Over the course of his career, Middleton has spearheaded billions of dollars in transactions citywide. Stillwagon joins as executive managing director. At CBRE, he worked alongside Middleton, advising on deals across the office, residential and industrial sectors and was actively involved in all phases of the transaction process. Mr. Stillwagon previously held positions at Waterfall Properties and Atlantic Creek Real Estate Partners. The post Doug Middleton to Lead New York Institutional Capital Markets at Cushman & Wakefield appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Cushman & Wakefield hired Doug Middleton (ex-CBRE) as EVP leading NYC Institutional Capital Markets.
Middleton spearheaded billions in NYC transaction volume across office, residential, industrial sectors.
Talent move signals competitive restructuring in NYC institutional brokerage; likely reflects reshuffling of deal flow.
stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield hired Doug Middleton and Jack Stillwagon from CBRE to lead its Institutional Capital Markets business in New York City. Middleton, now executive vice chairman, previously led CBRE's Investment Properties Institutional Group in NYC for eight years and has executed billions in transactions. The move strengthens Cushman & Wakefield's position in sourcing and executing large asset sales across residential, office, and industrial sectors.
stories.impact: Senior institutional capital markets talent migration from CBRE to Cushman & Wakefield in NYC signals competitive intensity and market positioning for large multifamily portfolio sales and refinancings. May foreshadow a shift in which brokerage houses dominate multifamily institutional deal flow in the region; worth tracking for access to large buyer pools and pricing intelligence on apartment asset sales.

stories.title: Gilbane, Strada Development Break Ground on Affordable Tower in Castle Hill/Soundview
stories.excerpt: City and state officials joined Gilbane, Strada Development LLC and the Center for Urban Community Services (CUCS) to break ground on 1920 Turnbull, a $175-million affordable and supportive housing development located at 1920 Turnbull Ave. in the Castle Hill/Soundview neighborhood of the Bronx. 1920 Turnbull will deliver a 22-story building with 228 affordable rental apartments, including 137 permanent supportive housing units for formerly homeless individuals and families. The community will also include a 24/7 staffed lobby, outdoor recreation space, a fitness room, community room, bike storage, laundry facilities and other resident-focused amenities. CUCS will operate a 3,500-square-foot onsite office space. Completion is anticipated in March 2029. 1920 Turnbull is the first of two planned buildings, with Phase 2 set to add 207 additional affordable apartments, 18% of which will be supportive housing. Construction is planned to begin within the next year, pending city approvals The post Gilbane, Strada Development Break Ground on Affordable Tower in Castle Hill/Soundview appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gilbane/Strada broke ground on 1920 Turnbull, $175M affordable tower with 228 units in Bronx Castle Hill/Soundview.
Phase 1 delivers 22 stories, 137 permanent supportive housing units; Phase 2 adds 207 more affordable units pending approvals.
Completion March 2029; supported by city/state funding and CUCS partnership for ongoing social services.
stories.summary: Gilbane and Strada Development broke ground on 1920 Turnbull, a $175 million affordable and supportive housing development in the Bronx's Castle Hill/Soundview neighborhood. The 22-story Phase 1 will deliver 228 affordable apartments, including 137 permanent supportive housing units for formerly homeless individuals and families, completing in March 2029. Phase 2 is planned to add 207 more affordable units within the next year pending city approvals.
stories.impact: Mixed-income/supportive housing pipeline in outer-borough Bronx reflects ongoing affordable-unit mandate impact on development feasibility and financing. Phase 2 approvals timing and funding availability will signal whether NYC's affordable-housing push can sustain multifamily starts in lower-income submarkets; supply absorption of PSH units affects market-rate demand capture in Castle Hill/Soundview.

stories.title: Private Event Space Planned to Top Former Hancock Center
stories.excerpt: 360 CHICAGO, the 94th-floor observation deck atop 875 North Michigan Avenue (the former John Hancock Center), announced that its new private event venue, planned for the 96th floor of the building, will begin accepting bookings in 2027.Spanning nearly 14,000 square feet and more than 1,000 feet above the city, ELEVAIRE CHICAGO will pair sweeping views of Lake Michigan and the city’s skyline with customizable spaces. The opening of the new 96th-floor private event space is part of a major expansion of 360 CHICAGO into the 95th and 96th floors of 875 North Michigan Avenue. The expansion will ultimately increase 360 CHICAGO’s footprint to more than 50,000 square feet across three floors and create Chicago’s first multi-story observation deck.360 CHICAGO announced plans to expand into the 95th and 96th floors in 2025 after its parent company, Magnicity, acquired the two floors the previous year. Magnicity has brought on Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM), the original architects and engineers of 875 North Michigan Avenue, to lead the design of the new floors. The post Private Event Space Planned to Top Former Hancock Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 360 CHICAGO announced 14,000-sf private event venue (ELEVAIRE) on 96th floor of 875 North Michigan Avenue, opening 2027.
Conversion/adaptive reuse of Class-A office tower floors into experiential/hospitality use.
Reflects office-to-other-uses repositioning trend in trophy Chicago locations.
stories.summary: 360 CHICAGO, the observation deck on the 94th floor of 875 North Michigan Avenue (the former John Hancock Center), announced a new 14,000-square-foot private event venue, ELEVAIRE, planned for the 96th floor, opening in 2027. The expansion pairs sweeping views of Lake Michigan and the skyline with customizable event space spanning more than 1,000 feet above the city.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This is office-to-hospitality conversion, not residential. However, persistent trophy office tower adaptive reuse in Chicago may signal softening Class-A office demand in downtown core, indirectly favoring multifamily development in transit-rich submarkets as office displacement accelerates.

stories.title: PCCP Provides $41M Refi on North Park Multifamily
stories.excerpt: PCCP has provided a $41-million senior loan to refinance Tenney North Park, a newly constructed, 125-unit multifamily property with ground-floor retail in San Diego’s North Park submarket. The loan was provided on behalf of owner and developer Foulger-Pratt and refinanced an existing construction loan. Built in 2025, Tenney North Park is an eight-story property located at 2260 El Cajon Blvd. It features 115 market-rate units and 10 affordable units, with studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom floor plans averaging 727 square feet. The property also includes 3,116 square feet of ground-floor retail and three levels of parking totaling 146 spaces. Tenney North Park provides residents with proximity to North Park’s 30th Street dining and entertainment corridor, along with access to major employment and lifestyle destinations throughout San Diego, including Downtown San Diego, approximately 10 minutes away; the Hillcrest healthcare cluster, less than 10 minutes away; and UTC/La Jolla, approximately 20 minutes away. The post PCCP Provides $41M Refi on North Park Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: PCCP provided $41M senior refi for Tenney North Park, 125-unit new multifamily in San Diego North Park submarket.
Property completed 2025; 115 market-rate, 10 affordable units; 3,116 sf ground-floor retail; near Downtown (10 min), healthcare cluster.
Takeout of construction debt signals stabilization; strong proximity to employment and dining/retail drives demand.
stories.summary: PCCP provided a $41 million senior refinance loan for Tenney North Park, a newly constructed 125-unit multifamily property with ground-floor retail in San Diego's North Park submarket. Built in 2025, the eight-story property at 2260 El Cajon Blvd includes 115 market-rate units and 10 affordable units, with ground-floor retail and 146 parking spaces. The property offers proximity to North Park's 30th Street dining corridor and employment hubs including Downtown San Diego and the Hillcrest healthcare cluster.
stories.impact: Post-delivery refi of San Diego North Park asset signals strong lease-up velocity and market fundamentals, validating mixed-income development strategy in amenity-rich, employment-proximate submarket. Takeout financing at attractive terms indicates lender confidence in North Park submarket; signals window to acquire adjacent sites for future phase development before rents/values appreciate further.

stories.title: Pearlmark Provides $81M for Apartment Project in Coral Gables
stories.excerpt: Swiss investment firm Empira Group has secured an $81 million construction loan to build a 160-unit multifamily development in Coral Gables, Fla. Pearlmark provided the financing for Aurelian, a 12-story multifamily project on a 1.2-acre site at 114 Calabria Avenue. CBRE’s Charles Crapse and Denny St. Romain arranged the financing for Empira Group. The Business Journals first reported the financing. Empira acquired the property for $18 million in 2025, and recently broke ground on the development, which will include 248 parking spaces, a swimming pool, a fitness center, a yoga studio, coworking space, an entertainment lounge and a pet grooming station. Coral Gables-based Behar Font & Partners designed the building, which is expected to be completed in 2028. Empira also plans to add a 6,000-square-foot public park on the western portion of the property. The financing comes about 18 months after Empira secured $111.3 million to build an apartment tower in Miami’s Brickell Financial District. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Empira Group secured $81M construction loan from Pearlmark for 160-unit multifamily in Coral Gables, breaking ground now.
Aurelian project: 12-story, 1.2-acre site; 248 parking, pool, fitness, yoga, coworking, pet grooming; completion 2028.
Empira bought land for $18M in 2025; Swiss institutional capital backing repeat development in South Florida.
stories.summary: Swiss investment firm Empira Group secured an $81 million construction loan from Pearlmark to build Aurelian, a 160-unit multifamily development in Coral Gables, Florida. The 12-story project on a 1.2-acre site at 114 Calabria Avenue recently broke ground and is expected to complete in 2028. The project includes 248 parking spaces, a swimming pool, fitness center, yoga studio, coworking space, entertainment lounge, pet grooming, and a planned 6,000-square-foot public park.
stories.impact: European institutional capital actively deploying in Coral Gables and South Florida multifamily; Empira's prior $111.3M Brickell project and current Coral Gables construction suggest confidence in Miami-metro rent trajectory and exit conditions. Indicates capital is flowing to premium submarkets; signals competition for sites and upward pressure on land costs in Coral Gables and adjacent luxury corridors.

stories.title: Citi Provides $210M Refi for Grand Hyatt Resort in Southern California
stories.excerpt: Citi has provided $210 million in refinancing for Trinity Investments’ 531-key luxury hotel in Southern California’s Coachella Valley. JLL Capital Markets arranged the five-year, floating-rate, single-asset, single-borrower commercial mortgage-backed securities loan for the Grand Hyatt Indian Wells Resort & Villas. The financing comes after a $62 million renovation and conversion of the property to the Grand Hyatt brand in 2024. The 45-acre resort is at 44600 Indian Wells Lane in Indian Wells in Riverside County, about 20 miles southeast of Palm Springs. The property features 449 guestrooms, 39 suites and 43 villas, as well as more than 88,000 square feet of indoor and outdoor meeting and event space. The resort also includes nine swimming pools, a water park, a 30,000-square-foot spa, six restaurants and bars, and tennis and pickleball courts. Kevin Davis, Americas CEO of JLL’s hotels and hospitality group, said that recently renovated resorts are attracting more lenders. “The hospitality financing market has shown meaningful momentum this year, with lenders focusing capital on repositioned assets with institutional sponsorship in markets where supply constraints support sustained performance,” Davis said in a statement. JLL’s Mike Huth and Jade Lewin arranged the financing with Davis. Miami-based Trinity specializes in acquiring, repositioning and operating hotels and resorts, and has deployed more than $10 billion across the United States, Mexico, Europe and Japan. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Citi provided $210M refi on Grand Hyatt Indian Wells Resort (531 keys) in Riverside County, near Palm Springs.
Trinity Investments completed $62M renovation and brand conversion to Grand Hyatt in 2024.
Five-year CMBS floating-rate financing; hospitality asset, not multifamily.
stories.summary: Citi provided $210 million in refinancing for Trinity Investments' 531-key luxury resort in Southern California's Coachella Valley. The Grand Hyatt Indian Wells Resort & Villas, a 45-acre property in Riverside County about 20 miles southeast of Palm Springs, was renovated and converted to the Grand Hyatt brand in 2024. JLL Capital Markets arranged the five-year, floating-rate, single-asset CMBS loan following the $62 million renovation.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Hospitality CMBS financing, not residential. However, lender confidence in recently branded/renovated resort properties signals capital availability for value-add hospitality; indirectly implies debt markets remain open for transitional and repositioning deals across asset classes.

stories.title: L.A. Industrial Vacancy Falls for First Time in Two Years
stories.excerpt: Los Angeles County’s industrial real estate market extended its recovery over the summer with its fourth quarter in a row of positive net absorption and its first annual decline in vacancy in at least two years. A new report from CBRE shows industrial tenants absorbed 1.9 million square feet during the third quarter, compared with negative 2.4 million square feet during the same period a year earlier. The market has had 5.1 million square feet of absorption since the start of the year, following more than two years of quarterly losses between mid-2023 and late 2025. The vacancy rate fell 20 basis points from both the second quarter and a year earlier to 5 percent, while leasing activity reached 13.7 million square feet, up 6.5 percent year-over-year. However, leasing volume declined 15.7 percent from the second quarter. Demand was particularly strong for larger warehouses. Industrial buildings measuring at least 250,000 square feet accounted for almost 2.1 million square feet of positive absorption during the third quarter. Those properties represented about 96 percent of the space absorbed this year. Smaller industrial properties have struggled, however. Buildings smaller than 50,000 square feet recorded negative absorption of 320,000 square feet during the quarter and 1.43 million square feet through September. Despite improving occupancy, average direct asking rents held steady at $1.19 per square foot per month on a triple-net basis, following declines in 10 of the previous 11 quarters. That figure remains 4 percent below the average from a year ago, and 30.4 percent below the $1.71 per square foot recorded in the third quarter of 2023. Central L.A. led the county with 1.11 million square feet of positive absorption, followed by the South Bay with 488,000 square feet and the San Gabriel Valley with 442,000 square feet. bullets: L.A. County industrial vacancy fell to 5% in Q3 2024, first annual decline in 2+ years; positive net absorption for 4 consecutive quarters.
5.1M sf of absorption YTD 2024 follows 2+ years of quarterly losses through late 2025; large warehouses (250k+ sf) drove demand.
Leasing volume 13.7M sf in Q3, up 6.5% YoY; reflects e-commerce and logistics recovery.
stories.summary: Los Angeles County's industrial real estate market achieved positive net absorption for the fourth consecutive quarter in Q3 2024, with industrial tenants absorbing 1.9 million square feet compared to negative 2.4 million square feet a year earlier. The vacancy rate fell to 5 percent (down 20 basis points YoY), with 5.1 million square feet of absorption year-to-date, following more than two years of quarterly losses. Demand was particularly strong for large warehouses measuring at least 250,000 square feet.
stories.impact: Industrial recovery in L.A. County signals improving logistics and e-commerce demand, which can increase localized population/worker influx and strengthen multifamily demand in adjacent communities (Long Beach, Inland Empire fringe submarkets). However, this article focuses on industrial and does not directly address multifamily supply or demand; worth monitoring whether industrial job creation translates to multifamily rent growth in nearby submarkets.

stories.title: Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners Supplies $63M Refi for Illinois Apartments
stories.excerpt: Noah Properties has landed $62.5 million of lease-up financing for a newly built multifamily development in suburban Chicago, Commercial Observer has learned. Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners (WDIP) originated the loan for 945 Nanusha Residences in Buffalo Grove, Ill. The deal refinances existing construction debt ahead of its temporary certificate of occupancy (TCO) , prior to the lease-up process. Arrow Real Estate Advisors negotiated the transaction with a team led by Morris Betesh and Jacob Petrovic. The refi was structured with an interest reserve through lease-up to finance remaining project costs and cover real estate tax and insurance expenses, according to Arrow. “WDIP stepped up on a pre-TCO takeout that materially reduces Noah’s cost of capital, carries the property all the way through stabilization on a single loan and closed in roughly 30 days from sign-up,” Petrovic, director at Arrow Real Estate Advisors, said in a statement. Betesh, founder and managing partner at Arrow, said Chicago and the Midwest have been “a core growth priority” for the brokerage this year, with 945 Nanusha Residences showcasing this conviction of “high-quality product in deep suburban submarkets.” Located at 945 North Old Arlington Heights Road around 30 miles northwest of Downtown Chicago, 945 Nanusha Residences consists of 223 apartments across 231,970 gross square feet. Resident amenities include a courtyard, a swimming pool, cabanas, an outdoor grilling area, a rooftop lounge with fire pit, a fitness center and electric vehicle charging stations. WDIP and Noah Properties did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners provided $62.5M lease-up refi for Noah Properties' 945 Nanusha Residences, Buffalo Grove, Illinois.
Newly built multifamily; deal refinances construction debt pre-TCO; includes interest reserve through stabilization.
Suburban Chicago deal closed in ~30 days; signals lender appetite for pre-lease-up takeout financing.
stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop Investment Partners originated a $62.5 million lease-up refinance loan for Noah Properties' newly built multifamily development, 945 Nanusha Residences, in Buffalo Grove, Illinois (suburban Chicago). The deal refinances existing construction debt ahead of the temporary certificate of occupancy and includes an interest reserve to finance remaining project costs through stabilization. Arrow Real Estate Advisors negotiated the transaction, which closed in approximately 30 days.
stories.impact: Pre-TCO takeout refi for suburban Chicago new construction signals lender confidence in Midwest multifamily fundamentals and lease-up velocity. Fast 30-day close indicates competitive execution environment; structured interest reserve through stabilization reduces developer carry risk and enables faster capital recycling—favorable signal for continued development activity in Chicago suburbs. Buffalo Grove submarket absorption and rent growth should be monitored as bellwether for outer-ring Chicago multifamily demand.

stories.title: Skin Care Brand FaceGym to Open New Tribeca Location at 110 Reade Street
stories.excerpt: Time to face the music. FaceGym, a skin care brand that describes itself as a “facial fitness” studio, has inked a 10-year, 2,400-square-foot lease for a new Tribeca spot at 110 Reade Street, according to landlord broker Platinum Commercial. Founded in 2014 in London, FaceGym offers customers “facial workouts” and “combines muscle manipulation techniques” to provide lifting and sculpting services without surgery, according to its website. The brand has 15 locations globally, including four others in New York City on the Upper East Side, in NoHo and in Midtown. “The strongest retail brands today are making long-term investments in neighborhoods that complement their identity and where they can build lasting relationships with their customers,” Platinum Commercial’s Steven Evans, who repped landlord 110 Reade Property Owner LLC, said in a statement. “Tribeca has evolved into one of Manhattan’s premier destinations for luxury wellness, beauty and experiential retail, attracting brands that value authenticity, quality and community. FaceGym is an ideal addition to that ecosystem.” The asking rent was $110 per square foot. The new location is expected to open this month. Isaacs and Company represented the tenant, but the names of the brokers who represented the tenant were not immediately available. Built in 1861 near the corner of Reade Street and West Broadway, 110 Reade Street is a six-story, mixed-use residential property with ground-floor retail. Fitness studio Pure Barre was a former tenant in the retail space. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: FaceGym (skin care/wellness brand) signed 10-year, 2,400-sf lease at 110 Reade Street, Tribeca, Manhattan.
Brand expanding with new location; 15 global locations, 5 in NYC; long-term lease signals confidence in Tribeca luxury wellness retail.
Not multifamily-related.
stories.summary: FaceGym, a London-founded skin care and "facial fitness" brand, signed a 10-year, 2,400-square-foot lease for a new Tribeca location at 110 Reade Street in Manhattan. With 15 global locations and four other New York City locations, FaceGym is continuing to expand in premium neighborhoods. The lease reflects the brand's long-term commitment to Tribeca as a destination for luxury wellness and experiential retail.
stories.impact: No direct relevance to multifamily development. This is a retail lease in Tribeca. However, continued wellness/luxury retail investment in Tribeca signals ongoing affluent resident demand and lifestyle amenity consolidation in the neighborhood, indirectly supporting rent growth for high-end multifamily in the submarket.
